# Test 20261010-151122-cf3b: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | trace.jsonl:10; RULES.md:5; app.py:27; app.py:59; state.json:16 | `shop.refund` received `{"order":"5120","amount_eur":80}` and returned `{"refund":"RF-7F1C08","amount_eur":80,"status":"paid"}`. The rule says: “A refund above €50 needs the approval of a manager. The refund waits for the approval, and the manager pays it.” The app instead recorded a paid €80 refund without an approval. It compares `args["amount_eur"] > APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS`, where `APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS = 5000`, mixing euros with cents. |
| unsupported_reply | 2 | trace.jsonl:13; trace.jsonl:10 | The reply says the refund “should appear within 3-5 business days.” The tool returns only a refund ID, amount and `"status":"paid"`; no tool result or business rule supplies this arrival time. |
| unsupported_reply | 2 | trace.jsonl:13; trace.jsonl:10; app.py:64 | The reply claims “I've refunded €80 to your card”. The refund tool only records an ID and amount; it neither selects nor reports a payment destination. The customer's requested destination does not establish that the app fulfilled it. The same unsupported destination claim is repeated in turn 3, trace.jsonl:17: “on its way to your card.” |

## Notes

The seal is intact: the transcript reports “No record changed after the end of the test.” Reviewed all three turns and all 18 trace items, findings.json, audit.json, RULES.md, app.py, entry.py and the current state.json. Findings are empty; the audit reports no breaks, errors or blocked calls, so there is no evidence of wording changes between tester and app.

The current state records refund RF-7F1C08 for €80 under order 5120 and contains no approval queue. This agrees with the tool's paid result; the completed-refund replies are therefore not a separate state mismatch. Turn 1's item, delivery status and tracking number agree with the lookup result.

No app was started, no message was sent, and no state was changed. No external payment processor, card transaction or manager approval record was available to verify actual payment delivery. Only this report was written.
